prompt:
Create ONE original transparent item-component sheet for our dark survival RPG Ashveil: exactly SIX separate artificial prosthetic OBJECTS in a clear 3-column by 2-row layout. Do not include people, human arms or legs, flesh, skin, cut stumps, blood, a mannequin, clothing, weapons, labels, diagrams, or extra objects. These are detached wood/metal/glass/relic prosthetic objects for inventory and later source-fragment mounting. This sheet is only ONE authored oblique/front object view of each item, NOT four directions or animation.

Use reference 1 (our own Culler salvage icon sheet) for the high-detail original game MATERIAL STYLE: hard-edged deliberate pixel-like contours, readable broad masses, chipped ash-gray worn iron, old tarnished yellow-brown brass fittings, dark warm leather, restrained ivory highlights, gritty earthy survival materials. Do NOT copy the six Culler item shapes, hooked weapon blades, power core shape or green tanks. Reference 2 is our own old32px item atlas: only the old prosthetic shapes at coordinates given below are semantic identity hints, not the desired resolution or quality. Redraw every object with substantially clearer material and real visible fittings. No external game pixels. Lighting is consistent upper-left, no emitted light or magical glow.

Exact layout:
TOP LEFT — Item.PegLeg: the wooden peg prosthesis (old atlas frame416,320,32,32). A wide hollow padded leather-and-iron attachment cuff at the TOP, a sturdy worn brown turned wood tapered peg below it, iron reinforcing collar, and one blunt visibly worn ground-contact end at the BOTTOM. It has no articulated knee, no toes and no fake human foot. Make the proximal cuff rim/inside socket and its axial center legible, with the wood shaft visibly entering its metal collar. Complete detached wood object.
TOP MIDDLE — Item.ArticulatedLeg (old frame448,320,32,32): a utilitarian iron-and-brass lower-leg prosthesis. Broad padded proximal attachment cuff at TOP; connected solid struts and an exposed round hinge/pin; clearly visible separate mechanical ankle hinge near the bottom; a small flat grounded metal foot with an unmistakable sole and modest toe at BOTTOM. It is a complete connected object, not an exploded diagram. No human thigh. Keep the ankle connection uncovered so a future distal foot source fragment can be identified without inventing an extra painted joint. Keep the actual proximal cuff/shaft/ankle/sole distinct.
TOP RIGHT — Item.HookHand (old frame480,320,32,32): a SHORT wrist prosthesis, not a whole forearm. Its dark leather-and-iron proximal wrist attachment cuff is at TOP, connected by a short obvious metal wrist stem to ONE thick curved iron hook below. Show a real cuff opening and stem connection, a blunt inner curve and a clear actual hook tip. The hook is not a painted human palm or fingers and is not an axe or sword. No biological hand, glove, thumb, or ordinary hand grip.
BOTTOM LEFT — Item.GlassEye (old frame0,352,32,32): ONE artificial cosmetic GLASS EYE, not an electronic eye or a relic machine. A rounded off-white/milky glass eyeball with a small dark brown-charcoal artificial iris/pupil, quiet pale glass specular highlights, subtly worn glass surface and clear dimensional rim. It must look like a small crafted glass object with a legible centered iris; no eyelid, flesh, optic nerve, wires, brass cage, glowing light, extra eyeball or floating magic. The game Def is glass-repairable, cosmetic, and does not restore sight; do not imply powered vision.
BOTTOM MIDDLE — Item.PioneerArm (old frame32,352,32,32): an ancient compact brass-and-iron artificial FOREARM with a broad real proximal elbow attachment cuff at TOP, connected plated forearm and cable/needle-tool housing, an EXPOSED clear mechanical wrist pin/ring, and an actual small mechanical gripping CLAW at BOTTOM. The claw has two opposing metal jaws with a visible gap and real jaw hinges, not a human hand or palm. Make the wrist and distal claw connection distinct enough to identify a source fragment later. Do not paint an upper arm or shoulder. It remains a tangible metal object with no glow even when depleted, and the picture does not assert that it is currently powered.
BOTTOM RIGHT — Item.GardenerLimb (old frame64,352,32,32): ONE strange pale ivory Y-shaped graft branch, between aged bone-like ceramic and smooth white wood, with subtle desaturated green mineral seams, a stout single proximal stem at TOP and two distinct curved branch-prongs toward the BOTTOM. Add one clearly identifiable weathered dark attachment BAND around the proximal stem near the top; its complete rim and center are visible so the graft's intended mounting end is unambiguous. Preserve its uncanny pale branching identity rather than making a normal flesh limb, articulated robot hand, antler trophy, or bunch of human bones. The two distal forks stay part of the same original object, no hidden duplicate branch.

All six objects are complete, comfortably centered inside separate grid cells, with generous FULLY TRANSPARENT space around every item and between cells. No object may cross a cell boundary or touch another. Keep material detail subordinate to strong distinctive silhouettes that remain understandable at24px and32px inventory size: tall brown peg; gray jointed metal foot; dark curved wrist hook; round pale glass eye; brass/iron forearm claw; pale Y-branch. No floor, no drop shadow or contact shadow, no framing, no fog/vignette/background wash, no text/numbers/arrows/sockets guides. RGBA background must be fully transparent. Render only these six original objects in a polished detailed gritty game-pixel style compatible with our own referenced material palette.
